name: GeoTech · Physical AI Hacks
headline: Hold my beer
summary: A real robot arm picks up a can when someone says "hold my beer": from a taped mark, or from a person's hand if that passes 8 of 10 by 11:00. Behind the demo, webcam and headset capture bring real people into nine simulated robot tables, because robots that work with people need to learn from real people.
goal: Hold My Beer: a person hands a MakerMods Maker Arm their drink and it takes it, backed by human interaction captured in Unreal across parallel simulated tables.
stack: Maker Arm SDK, Dream-1 in Unreal simulation, Isaac Sim physics, XR and webcam capture, scripted voice lines, optional LiveKit room
deadline_label: Demos due Sunday, Nov 8, 3 PM PT
today_note: Proposed means drafted overnight and not yet agreed. Confirm at the 9 AM standup.

today.detail: Hardware and e-stop check: name the e-stop person before anything is powered. Pull the latest code and run python3 -m handoff.preflight; NO-GO for the untaught poses is expected before teaching.
Settle the decisions below. Name the submission owner.

today.what: Teach and run the taped mark first
today.detail: Teach the arm its poses, calibrate the grip on the demo can, then 10 taped-mark trials (aim to lock by about 10:15). Hand trials only if the preflight says GO. Sim polish, voice lines, script and deck in parallel.
The taped mark is the live beat unless hand mode reached 8 of 10 trials. Post the call on the dashboard.
Tag the code and commit the taught arm poses. Nothing new after this.
A clean take of the demo in case the live run fails.
About 2 hours reserved (agreed). Video uploaded by 1:45, submitted by 2:30 (proposed).
Everyone on site. Demos are judged at 3 PM.

decisions.why: Nothing runs on the real arm without a named person on the stop button. Proposed: name them at the 8:30 hardware check, before anything is powered.

decisions.q: Who owns the submission, and when exactly is it due?
decisions.why: About 2 hours are reserved. The organizers haven't published the cutoff.

decisions.q: Fist bump: in or out, and who owns it?
decisions.why: FADI owns taking the can. The fist bump after it has no owner.

decisions.q: How do Dream and the coding agent split the real arm?
decisions.why: Today a local routine drives the real arm and Dream drives the simulated arms.

decisions.q: Is the voice agent still a must-have?
decisions.why: It was called a must-have on Saturday, then left out of the evening notes. Proposed: scripted lines with recorded backup audio.

decisions.q: Is the automatic pause, when someone gets in the arm's way, a must-have for the demo?
decisions.why: If yes, it needs an owner and a dry run on the arm controller. It is a software pause; the e-stop stays the safety stop.
